newsitem.title: JAPAN: Tokyo naphtha firmer on crude, traders sidelined.
newsitem.headline: Tokyo naphtha firmer on crude, traders sidelined.

text.p: Tokyo naphtha gained ground following overnight crude surges sparked by news that Iraq fired missiles at U.S. fighter planes, but players kept to the sidelines unsure of crude direction, traders said on Thursday.
"Whenever crude prices make a drastic move like this, naphtha dealers just stick to the sidelines," one trader said.
Open-spec naphtha for second-half November was assessed bid at $204.00, and offered at $206.00, compared to late Wednesday's $202.00/$202.50.
First-half November was quoted at $204.25/$206.50, up from Wednesday's $202.50/$203.00.
In naphtha spreads, bids for first-half November/first-half December were indicated at plus $1.00, while offers were assessed at plus $1.50 to $2.00.
Traders said Naphtha activity would pick up on Friday as most market players who attended the Asia-Pacific Petroleum Conference in Singapore would be back in Tokyo.
Talks for spot kerosene imports are expected to start as early as mid-October for late November or December delivery, middle distillate traders said.
Last year, kerosene imports got into full swing in December, they added. -- Tokyo Commodities (81-3 3432 8837)
